Commentary.Commentary: We are back for the all-important chase! The India Women players are in a huddle where Harmanpreet Kaur is giving a last-minute pep talk before they spread out and take their respective field positions. Out comes the South Africa Women's openers - Laura Wolvaardt and the in-form Tazmin Brits. The new ball is in the hands of young Kranti Gaud, who can move it both ways. All set - Here we go!
... THE RUN CHASE ...

The chase is now set at 252, and while the momentum has shifted firmly towards India, the game remains evenly poised. The South African batters are more than capable of handling this target, and they will back themselves to chase it down. All eyes now turn to the South Africa Women's pursuit of the target. Stay tuned...

Chloe Tryon is in for a chat. She says that she was trying to attack the stumps. Add that the conditions are a bit slow and the plan was to keep it wide and slow to some of the batters, which worked. Ends by saying that they didn't mind getting hit as it also brought the results and hopes that they can chase this one down.

The true turning point, however, came with the scintillating 88-run partnership between Ghosh and Sneh Rana, forged in just 53 deliveries. Rana played a crucial cameo of 33, allowing Ghosh to unleash a flurry of boundaries. Richa Ghosh's magnificent World Cup innings culminated in her dismissal for 94 in the final over, ensuring India had a truly competitive total on the board. The South Africa Women will certainly be disappointed, having initially dominated the innings with an excellent start. Chloe Tryon led the bowling charge for South Africa Women, taking 3/32. Marizanne Kapp, Nadine de Klerk, and Nonkululeko Mlaba each claimed two wickets

It was a remarkable recovery for the India Women, who hauled themselves from a precarious position of 102/6 to post a commanding total of 251. The innings began cautiously with Pratika Rawal and Smriti Mandhana, but Mandhana's dismissal in the 11th over heralded a middle-order collapse. Wickets tumbled at regular intervals, leaving the team in serious trouble until Amanjot Kaur and the dynamic Richa Ghosh arrived at the crease. Their 51-run partnership provided the initial stability, though Amanjot's 13 off 44 balls was primarily an anchor role.

Commentary.Commentary: Done with all the pre-match rituals! Laura Wolvaardt, skipper of South Africa Women, has a few last words before her team steps on the field. Smriti Mandhana and Pratika Rawal walk in with their blades for the India Women. Marizanne Kapp will start with the new ball. Away we go...

We are all set for the game to begin. The flags of both nations unfurl in the middle as the two sets of players, followed by the match officials, line up for their national anthems. The national anthem of South Africa will be played first, followed by that of India.

Harmanpreet Kaur, the captain of India Women, says that they would have bowled first as well, but the toss is not in their hands and they have been losing a lot of them. Adds that now they will focus on setting a good total. Mentions that the support has been great and they just want to play good cricket. Tells that every game is important for them and they need to keep showing improvement in each one of them. Informs that Amanjot Kaur is back in the team in place of Renuka Singh Thakur.

Laura Wolvaardt, the skipper of South Africa Women, says that the wicket looks good, and with a bit of weather around, they want to chase here.
